item.title: Shimane Leisure Guide: Garden Therapy, Lake Cruises & Mythology Trails
item.description: Shimane moves at a slower frequency than Japan’s major tourist circuits. There are no theme parks, no neon-lit shopping districts. What it offers instead — a garden ranked number one in Japan for over two decades, sunsets named among the country’s hundred most beautiful, boat rides through feudal samurai districts, and coastal paths connecting the birthplaces of Japanese mythology — requires patience and rewards it generously. Adachi Museum of Art: How to See It Right The Adachi Museum of Art in Yasugi is not primarily a museum.

item.title: Shiga Onsen Guide: Lakefront Hot Springs & Mountain Retreats
item.description: Shiga Prefecture is not the first name that comes to mind when Japanese travelers discuss onsen destinations. That oversight benefits the visitor who does their homework. Unlike the heavily marketed hot spring towns of Beppu, Hakone, or Kinosaki, Shiga’s hot spring accommodations exist in a state of relative calm — genuinely local clientele, smaller facilities, and a setting that combines the therapeutic ritual of the bath with some of the most striking lakeside and mountain scenery in central Honshu.
